a quantitative assessment of the compliance of business processes with the requirements of ISO 9000 is possible even in early stage of design of the quality management system.

the 80‐20 principle and the inventive problem‐solvingsystem can be applied for the design of highly mature quality management system (ISO 9001: 2000).Originality/value – This is one of the first papers in the literature that applies the 80‐80 principle and inventive problem‐solving methodology in the context of ISO 9000 standard.

(a) ISO 9001 requirements are not of equal importance in terms of their value to the organization; (b) the most important requirements of the ISO 9001 standard are those that are related to the customer; (c) the requirements that are related to internal processes are of less importance, while requirements related to the management system and documentation are of the least importance to the organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the identification of the critical requirements of ISO 9000:2000 standard; (ii) the identification of conflicts and barriers in the process of implementing ISO 9000 standard; (iii) the identification of innovative solutions to the problems that arise from the analysis of conflicts and barriers; and (iv) the identification of vectors of innovation for supporting quality management system design and implementation in ISO 9000 framework.
the development and validation of a model of the determinants of quality management system effectiveness.
the development of a new methodology for identifying and managing the most critical aspects of QMS design and implementation, in the framework of an innovative approach to the ISO 9001 standard.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality management system is not a static system but rather a dynamic one that should be constantly updated and improved in order to meet the ever-changing demands of the business environment.
ISO 9001 is a good framework, but not a sufficient one.
the ISO 9000:2000 standard provides a good foundation to build a quality management system that will help a company improve its performance and achieve its goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ISO 9001 standard can be used to support innovation in the organization.
the ISO 9001 standard has a significant impact on the quality management of the company.

we have proposed a new methodology to identify the critical issues, conflicts, and barriers in the QMS design and implementation process, as well as to define innovative solutions to the issues arising from the analysis of these conflicts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality management system is an effective tool for the management of innovation, but it must be implemented with a focus on the innovation process.
it is possible to identify and quantify the value weight of each ISO 9001 requirement in the equation of competitiveness.
the 80/20 rule is not only applicable to business but also to the field of science and engineering.
